## Abstract

::: {.abstract}
Infectious disease modelling has a long history, but the last ten years
changed what it is asked to do during an outbreak and how fast.
I open with that decade as I saw it.
The 2014 Ebola epidemic in West Africa, where real-time modelling arrived
in public view and so did its overreach.
COVID-19, where my group produced daily reproduction number estimates for
thousands of locations and weekly estimates for the UK government's
advisers.
Mpox in 2022, and the current outbreak of Ebola disease caused by
Bundibugyo virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Along the way I say what a modeller does during an outbreak and what keeps
going wrong.

The second part is about AI in two senses.
Coding agents now write most of the code I ship, including a live model of
the current outbreak.
I describe what that changes about how models get built and checked, and
what it does not.
I then place the other methods, universal differential equations,
normalising flows and time series foundation models, on a shared map
alongside the reinforcement learning and machine learning that later
speakers cover.

I close with an open question.
Where does AI fit in this work, and what stays with people?
:::

The organisers asked me to open the workshop with a keynote of 20 to 30
minutes under the tentative title *Infectious Disease Modelling in the Age
of AI*, with the content left to me.
Their suggestion was some history of infectious disease modelling, a few
practical examples from my own experience, and an open question on how AI
fits into this space going forward.
The audience is a mix of infectious disease and AI researchers, some with
little or no modelling background.
Steven Abrams and Pieter Libin speak straight after with an overview of
methods, followed by three case studies.

## Resources

### Outbreaks

- [BVDOutbreakSize][bvd].
  A live joint model of the 2026 DRC outbreak of Ebola disease caused by
  Bundibugyo virus, built largely with coding agents.
  [Source][bvd-repo].
- [The epiforecasts COVID-19 dashboard][covid].
  Daily $R_t$ estimates and forecasts, 2020 to 2022.
- [EpiNow2][epinow2].
  The real-time $R_t$ tool from the pandemic.

### Agents

- [How I am LLM][howillm].
  What coding agents do and do not do in a research workflow.
- [A workflow for infectious disease modelling][workflow].
  The workflow the agents are asked to follow.

### Composable modelling

- [What we want from an approach][approaches].
  The design considerations, and the two approaches we are taking.
- [EpiAware][epiaware].
  The Julia organisation building it.
- [JuliaCon 2026][juliacon].
